policy_title: Dismantle nuclear weapons and cancel Trident
stated: Push for the UK to sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), dismantle nuclear weapons, cancel the Trident programme, and remove all foreign nuclear weapons from UK soil.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Push for the UK to sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), and following this to begin immediately the process of dismantling our nuclear weapons, cancelling the Trident programme and removing all foreign nuclear weapons from UK soil.

bearing_set.reason: Dismantling Trident and removing nuclear weapons directly affects the UK's national security posture and defence deterrence capability, earning a real verdict on safety and security.

The Trident/Dreadnought programme sustains tens of thousands of skilled, well-paid defence-industry jobs (Faslane, AWE Aldermaston/Burghfield, BAE Systems, supply chain); cancellation would concentrate significant job-security losses on those workers and their communities.

The Dreadnought submarine renewal programme carries an estimated £31bn+ procurement cost and very large lifecycle spending; cancellation would remove a major future spending commitment, materially shifting the funded/borrowed balance and debt trajectory.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the policy's primary effect is on national security (O5); it has a large and direct fiscal consequence for public finances (O12); and the concentrated workforce employed in the nuclear programme faces material job-security harm (O4). Other fundamentals (housing, healthcare, environment, equality) are at most negligible or speculative second-order effects without a pinnable mechanism.
